import html # Predefined HTML template for the invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT: str = """ {title}

{title}

Date: {date}

Description

{description}
{notes_section} """ def generate_event_invite(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The name or title of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain multiple lines and formatting). date : str The scheduled date for the event. notes : str Extra information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Notes ----- All user-provided content is escaped to prevent XSS and other injection attacks. The function does not allow arbitrary HTML or script tags in the output. """ # Escape all user input to neutralize any potentially malicious content. safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description, quote=True) safe_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) # The notes section is optional; escape it if provided. if notes: safe_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=True) notes_section = f"""

Additional Notes

{safe_notes}

""" else: notes_section = "" # Build the final HTML using the predefined template. html_output = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( title=safe_title, date=safe_date, description=safe_description, notes_section=notes_section ) return html_output.strip()
